memberdef.name: exports
memberdef.initializer: = { listCategories, listPath, getDownloadTarget, searchEntries, listLatestReleases, peekRootSync, getRoot, }

briefdescription.para: The filesystem domain layer of the CloudAvid File Portal: resolves FILES_ROOT, sanitises every client-supplied path, walks the download tree, and turns the real disk into the data behind all of server.js's JSON and download APIs.

sect2.title: 🧒 ELI5 Summary
sect2.para: Imagine the portal is a library, and server.js is the librarian at the front desk. Where do the books actually live? In the basement. This file is the basement keeper: the only person with the key to the storage room.

The librarian never walks into the basement. When a visitor asks "what shelves do you have?" the librarian shouts downstairs, and the basement keeper walks the aisles, counts the books, checks the newest arrival dates, and sends a neat list back up. When a visitor asks "hand me that exact box", the basement keeper first checks the request slip very carefully — nobody is allowed to ask for the box marked .. ("two rooms back"), and nobody may leave the storage room. If anything is wrong — the basement is locked (FILES_ROOT missing), it is empty, or the slip is invalid — the keeper sends back a stamped slip of paper saying exactly why (403 PATH_TRAVERSAL, 503 FILES_ROOT_EMPTY, …), which the librarian forwards to the visitor.

listitem.para: Sole Owner of FILES_ROOT: Reads process.env.FILES_ROOT (populated from .env by lib/load-env.js), resolves it against the project root, and validates that it exists, is a directory, and is non-empty with at least one visible category folder. No other file in the repository resolves or stats FILES_ROOT except via this module.

Path Safety Wall: Converts any client-supplied relative path into a validated absolute path that is provably inside FILES_ROOT, rejecting . / .. segments and NUL bytes, and re-checking with path.relative() after resolution (defence in depth).
Directory Listing Engine: listCategories() (with per-category recursive summaries) and listPath() (flat listings at any depth) — the data behind /api/categories and /api/files.

Download Resolver: getDownloadTarget() stats a file and returns the { absPath, fileName, size, mtime } bundle that server.js streams with fs.createReadStream. This module never streams; it only decides what may be streamed.
Search Engine: searchEntries() — an iterative, depth-capped DFS over the tree with substring name matching, hard entry/limit caps and a truncated flag — the data behind /api/search.
Release Feed: listLatestReleases() — a full-tree walk that ranks every visible file by modification time — the data behind /api/releases.
Synchronous Health Probe: peekRootSync() — a never-throwing, synchronous snapshot of FILES_ROOT health for /api/health and the startup banner.
Structured Failure Contract: serviceError() stamps every failure with an httpStatus and a stable machine-readable code, which server.js's sendServiceError() forwards verbatim as JSON.
Hidden-Entry Filter: isHidden() enforces the portal-wide rule that index.html, index.php and dotfiles never appear in any listing anywhere in the product.

sect2.title: 🧭 Role in the Overall Architecture
sect2.para: This file is the bottom of the back-end and the only file that touches the downloads tree. The deliberate two-layer split of this project is:

listitem.para: server.js = transport layer (HTTP parsing, headers, CORS, streaming, routing, logging). Knows nothing about how paths are validated.

lib/files-service.js = domain layer (this file). Knows nothing about HTTP; it never writes headers and never sees a request object. Its only HTTP awareness is the httpStatus numbers it stamps onto errors, a pragmatic exception that lets server.js's generic catch render the right status without a mapping table.

sect2.para: Upward, it is consumed exclusively by server.js, which wires each exported function to exactly one API route. Downward, it depends only on Node built-ins (fs/promises, fs, path) and on the environment contract established by lib/load-env.js. The frontend never calls this module; it consumes its output indirectly through assets/js/services/resource-service.js.

What This File Does NOT Do:
It does not serve HTTP. No routing, no headers, no streaming — all of that is server.js (streamDownload, sendJSON).
It does not cache. Every call re-reads the disk; all caching in this product lives in the browser (resource-service.js's sessionStorage).
It does not enforce the browser-side isHidden() copy — that is a duplicated display-level filter in assets/js/browse.js and assets/js/services/resource-service.js. This module's filter is the authoritative one; the frontend ones are cosmetic backups.
It does not read or write file contents. It only stats, lists and resolves paths; even getDownloadTarget() returns metadata, and the bytes are streamed by server.js.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect1.title: 🏗️ Architectural Flow
sect1.para: The diagram below shows how one service call flows: every public function funnels through the same three gates — root resolution, structure validation (where applicable), and the path-safety wall — before any disk read happens.

sect1.title: 🔄 Execution Sequence
sect1.para: The sequence below traces the two most important runtime conversations: a browse request (category → folder → download) and a search, showing how server.js interleaves this module with its own transport helpers and how the browser arrives here via the frontend service layer.

sect2.title: 🧩 Block: Core Module Requires (fs/promises, fs, path)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Load the three Node built-ins this module is built from: the promise API for all async directory work, the callback/sync API for the one synchronous probe, and the path toolkit for every safety check.
🧒 ELI5
The basement keeper's three tools: a walkie-talkie that texts back later (fs/promises — "I'll tell you when the shelf count is done"), an instant-answer phone (fs — "right now: does the room exist, yes or no"), and a map of the building (path) so every route between rooms is drawn the same way on every operating system.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
fs/promises is required and bound to the name fs: every listing, stat and walk in this file is async and uses the promise API, which keeps the hot paths (concurrent Promise.all listings) composable.
The classic callback module is required separately as fsSync and used in exactly one place: peekRootSync(), which must run inside a synchronous request handler and inside the startup banner without async/await plumbing.
path is required once and powers every join, resolve, relative and separator handling decision — critical because FILES_ROOT may be a Windows path (D:\CloudAvid\Downloads per .env.example) while all API-facing paths are POSIX-style.
📥 Inputs
None (module loading only).
📤 Outputs
Three module-local bindings used by every other block in this file.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: Node.js runtime only — no npm dependency, which is why the domain layer keeps working even if node_modules is wiped.
Consumed by: nothing at require time; the bindings are used by all functions documented below.
Sideways: mirrors server.js's "built-ins first" require style and lib/load-env.js's identical approach.
server.js
lib/load-env.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
If fsSync is removed (e.g. during an async-only refactor), peekRootSync() throws a ReferenceError the first time /api/health is hit or the startup banner renders — health checks start reporting degraded and monitoring silently flips. Conversely, replacing require("fs/promises") with require("fs") breaks every await in this file at runtime: the calls return callbacks-style behaviour and all six API routes start 500-ing.
💻 Live Source Code:
constfs=require("fs/promises"); constfsSync=require("fs"); constpath=require("path");
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Block: Operational Limit Constants
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Centralise the guard-rail numbers that keep runaway directories, huge trees and over-broad searches from consuming unbounded time or memory.
🧒 ELI5
Speed limits posted at the basement door: "you may check at most 8000 boxes on one trip, you may descend at most 12 floors, you may put 200 search results on the trolley, and 12 items on the new-arrivals shelf." Posted once so every worker follows the same rules.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
MAX_WALK_ENTRIES = 8000 caps how many visible entries the search and release walks may visit; both loops stop mid-walk when reached.
MAX_WALK_DEPTH = 12 caps recursion/stack depth in summarizeTree, searchEntries and listLatestReleases; deeper directories are silently skipped rather than erroring.
SEARCH_LIMIT = 200 is the default and the hard maximum result count for searchEntries; a client-passed limit is clamped with Math.min so it can never raise the ceiling.
RELEASES_LIMIT = 12 is the default cap for listLatestReleases (hard maximum 50, enforced separately inside that function).
📥 Inputs
None (compile-time constants).
📤 Outputs
Bounds consumed by summarizeTree, searchEntries, listLatestReleases.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: nothing.
Consumed by: the three walking functions below; indirectly by the frontend (resource-service.js caps its own suggestion request at limit: 6, always under the ceiling).
assets/js/services/resource-service.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
These numbers are part of the observable behaviour of three API routes. Raising MAX_WALK_ENTRIES changes the worst-case latency of /api/search and /api/releases (a huge tree = slow responses on the request thread); lowering SEARCH_LIMIT below the frontend's request limits (e.g. limit=6 suggestions) silently truncates autocomplete. MAX_WALK_DEPTH interacts with the repository layout: deeper than 12 nested category folders will vanish from search and releases, which looks like a data bug, not a config change.
💻 Live Source Code:
constMAX_WALK_ENTRIES=8000; constMAX_WALK_DEPTH=12; constSEARCH_LIMIT=200; constRELEASES_LIMIT=12;
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: isHidden(name)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Define, in exactly one place, which filenames are invisible to the whole portal: index pages (which would leak as "files" next to real downloads) and every dotfile.
🧒 ELI5
The keeper's ignore-list taped inside the storage room door: anything called "index" and anything starting with a dot is scenery, not merchandise — even if a visitor asks for it by name, it is not on any shelf list.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
Coerce the argument with String(name || "") so undefined or empty names are treated as hidden rather than crashing a walk.
Lower-case once (l) so INDEX.HTML on a case-insensitive Windows volume is filtered identically to index.html.
Hide when: the name is falsy, or is index.html, or is index.php, or starts with . (catches .git, .env, .htaccess, and macOS .DS_Store).
Note the asymmetric test style: index.html/index.php compare the lower-cased string, while the dotfile check uses the original name — dotfiles are conventionally lower-case, and startsWith(".") is case-agnostic anyway.
📥 Inputs
name: a raw directory-entry name (string or falsy).
📤 Outputs
boolean — true means "skip this entry in every listing, walk and search result".
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: nothing.
Consumed by: readVisibleEntries, summarizeTree's walk, searchEntries, listLatestReleases's walk — i.e. every disk-reading path in this file.
Sideways: this is the authoritative copy of the rule. The frontend re-implements it defensively in resource-service.js (isHidden used by listFiles) and in browse.js (filtering API rows again at render time).
assets/js/services/resource-service.js
assets/js/browse.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
Adding a name here hides it from every surface at once — categories, listings, search, releases and download listings (though not downloads themselves, which go through getDownloadTarget and do not consult this function). Removing, say, the index.html rule makes web-server index files appear as downloadable products. Note the frontend has its own copies: changing only this function leaves browse.js still filtering the old list, so surfaces can disagree after a partial edit.
💻 Live Source Code:
functionisHidden(name){ constl=String(name||"").toLowerCase(); return!name||l==="index.html"||l==="index.php"||name.startsWith("."); }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: serviceError(httpStatus, code, message)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
The module's single error factory: every failure this file raises is an Error enriched with an HTTP status and a stable machine-readable code, forming the API's error contract.
🧒 ELI5
Pre-printed rejection slips. Instead of the keeper shouting "something went wrong!", every refusal gets a stamp: the desk knows how serious it is (the number) and a short code the visitor's software can recognise (like PATH_TRAVERSAL).
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
Construct a plain new Error(message) — the message becomes the human-readable error field of the JSON response.
Attach err.httpStatus — the status server.js's catch block uses as err.httpStatus || 500.
Attach err.code — a SCREAMING_SNAKE identifier that server.js forwards verbatim as the code field, letting the frontend (and humans reading API docs) branch on exact failure kinds.
No stack manipulation, no custom class — deliberately lightweight so ordinary instanceof Error checks and log formatting keep working.
📥 Inputs
httpStatus: number (400/403/404/503 in this file).
code: stable identifier — INVALID_PATH, PATH_TRAVERSAL, NOT_FOUND, NOT_A_DIRECTORY, NOT_A_FILE, FILES_ROOT_MISSING, FILES_ROOT_NOT_FOUND, FILES_ROOT_NOT_DIRECTORY, FILES_ROOT_EMPTY, FILES_ROOT_NO_CATEGORIES.
message: end-user-presentable sentence (surfaced verbatim in JSON).
📤 Outputs
An Error with httpStatus and code properties, meant to be thrown.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: nothing.
Consumed by: literally every throwing block in this file; and indirectly by server.js's sendServiceError(res, err), which reads exactly these two properties.
server.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
The code strings are a public API contract: resource-service.js's parseError() surfaces them to users and tests/monitors may match on them. Renaming a code (or changing an httpStatus) alters API responses with no compile-time signal. If a new failure path throws a plain Error instead of using this factory, server.js renders it as 500 INTERNAL — an accurate status but a debugging dead-end.
💻 Live Source Code:
functionserviceError(httpStatus,code,message){ consterr=newError(message); err.httpStatus=httpStatus; err.code=code; returnerr; }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: resolveConfiguredRoot(projectRoot)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Turn the raw FILES_ROOT environment string into an absolute directory path, failing fast with a dedicated error when the setting is absent.
🧒 ELI5
Reading the label on the basement door. No label? Refuse to guess — go back and tell the manager "the door has no name on it" (503 FILES_ROOT_MISSING). Label can be a full address or directions from the lobby; the keeper knows both dialects.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
Read process.env.FILES_ROOT — populated at boot by lib/load-env.js before server.js requires this module (both are required after loadEnv() runs, so ordering is safe).
Treat undefined, null and whitespace-only values ("" after String(raw).trim()) as "not configured" → throw 503 FILES_ROOT_MISSING. 503 (not 500) is deliberate: it tells the operator this is a configuration problem, and it reads correctly on /api/health-style probes.
Trim once into configured; whitespace around the value in .env is therefore harmless.
If the string is already absolute (path.isAbsolute — true for /srv/cloudavid/downloads on Linux and D:\CloudAvid\Downloads on Windows), resolve it with path.resolve(configured) to normalise separators and collapses.
Otherwise anchor it to the supplied projectRoot (__dirname of server.js) with path.resolve(projectRoot, configured) — this is why .env.example's relative default ./sample-downloads works from any working directory.
📥 Inputs
projectRoot: absolute base directory (always PROJECT_ROOT from server.js).
Environment: FILES_ROOT (documented in .env.example).
📤 Outputs
Absolute, normalised root path string.
Throws 503 FILES_ROOT_MISSING when unset/blank.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: process.env.FILES_ROOT (written by lib/load-env.js), Node path, serviceError.
Consumed by: getRoot (async path) and peekRootSync (sync path) — the only two call sites.
lib/load-env.js
.env.example
server.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
This is the seam between deployment configuration and the whole product. Renaming the FILES_ROOT key breaks every deployment's .env at once; removing the trim makes "D:\Downloads " (trailing space) resolve to a different directory on Windows; changing the relative-path anchor from projectRoot to process.cwd() breaks npm start from any other working directory and any service manager that starts the app from elsewhere. Security note: it intentionally does not validate what the path is — pointing FILES_ROOT at the source tree would expose the application itself, which is exactly what .env.example's comment warns against.
💻 Live Source Code:
functionresolveConfiguredRoot(projectRoot){ constraw=process.env.FILES_ROOT; if(raw==null||String(raw).trim()===""){ throwserviceError( 503, "FILES_ROOT_MISSING", "FILES_ROOTisnotset.Addittoyour.envfile." ); } constconfigured=String(raw).trim(); returnpath.isAbsolute(configured) ?path.resolve(configured) :path.resolve(projectRoot,configured); }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: getRoot(projectRoot)
🧩 Function: splitRel(relPath)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Normalise any client-supplied relative path into a clean array of segments — the input normaliser for the path-safety wall.
🧒 ELI5
Reading the visitor's scribbled directions and rewriting them as a clean list of room names: cross out blanks, fix back-slashes, drop the empty bits, and only then start walking.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
String(relPath || "") — undefined/null become an empty path (which callers interpret as "the root itself").
replace(/\\/g, "/") — accept Windows-style separators from clients (URLs or query strings may carry backslashes) and unify to POSIX.
split("/") then .map(p => p.trim()) — tolerate accidental spaces around segments ("my folder" survives as two clean segments).
.filter(Boolean) — drop empty segments, so trailing slashes (/api/files/docs/) and double slashes (docs//sub) never reach path.resolve as meaningful parts.
📥 Inputs
relPath: raw client path (string, possibly undefined, either separator style, possibly with empty segments).
📤 Outputs
Array of non-empty, trimmed segment strings ([] for the root).
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: nothing.
Consumed by: resolveInsideRoot exclusively.
assets/js/services/resource-service.js — the frontend's encodeRelPath() is the mirror-image producer: it also backslash-normalises, filters empties, then percent-encodes each segment before calling the API, so both ends agree on segment boundaries.
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
This function defines what a "path segment" means across the whole API surface. If the trim or filter steps disappear, /api/files/docs// starts producing a "" segment which path.resolve treats as harmless — but resolveInsideRoot's relPosix gains double slashes and the returned path values stop round-tripping through the frontend's browseHref/downloadHref builders. Removing the backslash swap makes any Windows-flavoured client path resolve to a single segment named docs\sub — a 404 that looks like missing data.
💻 Live Source Code:
functionsplitRel(relPath){ returnString(relPath||"") .replace(/\\/g,"/") .split("/") .map((p)=>p.trim()) .filter(Boolean); }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: resolveInsideRoot(root, relPath)
🧩 Function: toPosixRel(root, absPath)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Convert an absolute path that is already known to be inside the root back into the canonical POSIX relative path the API uses as the path field of every listed entry.
🧒 ELI5
Walking back from a real room to the storage-room door and writing down the turns you took — but in the same "aisle/shelf/box" shorthand every customer list is written in, no matter which operating system's dialect the floor plan uses.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
path.relative(root, absPath) — the OS-native relative walk (on Windows this may contain backslashes).
.split(path.sep) — split on the platform separator, not a literal slash, so Windows paths split correctly.
.filter(Boolean) — drop the empty segment produced when absPath is the root (so the root maps to [], and relPosix is "").
.join("/") — re-join with POSIX slashes: the canonical on-the-wire form that resource-service.js later re-encodes segment-by-segment for URLs.
📥 Inputs
root: validated root; absPath: an entry's absolute path produced by path.join(target, ent.name).
📤 Outputs
POSIX relative path string (e.g. docs/manuals/install-guide.pdf).
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: path.
Consumed by: listPath (building each entry's path field).
Sideways: complements splitRel/resolveInsideRoot — together they guarantee the path values this module emits are exactly the values it accepts back on the next request (a round-trip contract the frontend depends on for browseHref/downloadHref).
assets/js/services/resource-service.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
The output format is a cross-file contract: browse.js feeds these path strings back into /api/files/... and /api/download/..., and home.js builds download links from release paths. If backslashes ever leak into the output (e.g. replacing split(path.sep) with split("/")), Windows deployments break in a confusing way: listings render, but the encoded URL contains \\endiskip and the next request 404s — or worse, falls into resolveInsideRoot's backslash tolerance and traverses somewhere unintended.
💻 Live Source Code:
functiontoPosixRel(root,absPath){ returnpath.relative(root,absPath).split(path.sep).filter(Boolean).join("/"); }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: readVisibleEntries(dir)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
One-liner wrapper that reads a directory with entry types included and strips hidden entries — the standard "what can the visitor see here?" question.
🧒 ELI5
A quick glance at one shelf: read every label, but skip anything on the ignore-list taped to the door before showing the list to anyone.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
fs.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true }) returns Dirent objects — each carrying isDirectory() / isFile() without a per-entry stat round-trip. This is the cheap type source used everywhere.
.filter(e => !isHidden(e.name)) applies the portal-wide ignore list before anything downstream sees the entries.
Errors are not caught here: a missing/unreadable directory propagates to callers, which either translate it (404 in listPath) or swallow it (walks below).
📥 Inputs
dir: absolute directory path.
📤 Outputs
Promise of a filtered Dirent[].
Rejects with the raw fs error if dir is unreadable.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: fs/promises, isHidden.
Consumed by: assertCategoryStructure and listPath.
lib/files-service.js (walkers below intentionally duplicate the readdir+filter pattern inline so they can count/halt independently).
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
Removing withFileTypes: true breaks every caller silently: the filter callbacks would then receive plain strings, e.isDirectory would be undefined, and directories would be misclassified as skipped files — categories would disappear from the API with no error thrown. Adding a catch here would mask 404s in listPath (empty array instead of NOT_FOUND), breaking the frontend's error messaging.
💻 Live Source Code:
asyncfunctionreadVisibleEntries(dir){ constentries=awaitfs.readdir(dir,{withFileTypes:true}); returnentries.filter((e)=>!isHidden(e.name)); }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: assertCategoryStructure(root)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
Enforce the product's content contract: FILES_ROOT must contain at least one visible directory (a "category"), because the portal's information architecture is category-first.

🧒 ELI5
The librarian's rule for the basement: a storage room with no shelves isn't a library — it's a locked closet (503 FILES_ROOT_EMPTY), and a room with only loose paper on the floor isn't organised either (503 FILES_ROOT_NO_CATEGORIES): files directly in the root simply don't count as shelves.

⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)


readVisibleEntries(root) — hidden entries (including the stray index.html nginx-style deployments add) do not count.

visible.length === 0 → throw 503 FILES_ROOT_EMPTY with a message telling the operator the folder is not a valid resource repository.

visible.filter(e => e.isDirectory()) — only directories qualify as categories; loose files in the root are ignored by design (this is also why server.js's README-style files at FILES_ROOT root never appear in the UI).

dirs.length === 0 → throw 503 FILES_ROOT_NO_CATEGORIES, with a message that documents the rule itself ("Only directories are used
   as categories...") so the operator can self-serve.

Return the Dirent[] of category folders for reuse by the two callers (avoids a second readdir).



📥 Inputs


root: validated root directory.

Disk: FILES_ROOT top level.



📤 Outputs


Promise of visible directory Dirent[].

Throws 503 FILES_ROOT_EMPTY / FILES_ROOT_NO_CATEGORIES.



🔗 Project Dependencies


Depends on: readVisibleEntries, serviceError.

Consumed by: listCategories (returns them as the category list), listPath (root case), searchEntries and listLatestReleases (validating before walking).




server.js — these 503s are what the startup banner's peekRootSync state lines predict; a server that boots "green" but serves FILES_ROOT_NO_CATEGORIES means content was changed after start.

⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
This function defines what a category is. Allowing top-level files to count as categories changes /api/categories, /api/files, /api/search and /api/releases simultaneously, and the frontend's category-card grid (home.js) would render files as folders. Loosening the empty check (returning [] instead of throwing) turns the portal into a blank page instead of a clear operator error — the thrown 503s are a feature, deliberately surfaced through sendServiceError.

💻 Live Source Code:
asyncfunctionassertCategoryStructure(root){
constvisible=awaitreadVisibleEntries(root);
if(visible.length===0){
throwserviceError(
503,
"FILES_ROOT_EMPTY",
"FILES_ROOTisemptyandisnotavalidresourcerepository."
);
}
constdirs=visible.filter((e)=>e.isDirectory());
if(dirs.length===0){
throwserviceError(
503,
"FILES_ROOT_NO_CATEGORIES",
"FILES_ROOTcontainsnocategoryfolders.Onlydirectoriesareusedascategories;filesintherootareignored."
);
}
returndirs;
}


─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: summarizeTree(dir)
🧩 Function: listCategories(projectRoot)
🧩 Function: listPath(projectRoot, relPath)
🧩 Function: getDownloadTarget(projectRoot, relPath)
🧩 Function: nameMatches(name, query)
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
The single match predicate for search: case-insensitive substring test with an "empty query matches everything" escape hatch.
🧒 ELI5
"Does the label have these letters somewhere in it?" No letters typed? Then everything matches — the search box showing all files is a feature, not a bug.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
if (!query) return true; — an empty/undefined query matches every entry; combined with searchEntries's limit this makes /api/search?q= a cheap "first 200 files" explorer.
String(name).toLowerCase().includes(query) — the query arrives already lower-cased and trimmed (normalised once in searchEntries), so the per-entry cost is one toLowerCase and one includes. Substring semantics (not word-prefix) mean searching fox finds firefox-installer.zip.
📥 Inputs
name: an entry name; query: already-lower-cased search text or empty.
📤 Outputs
boolean.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: nothing.
Consumed by: searchEntries (both the directory-name branch and the file-name branch).
Sideways: the frontend does no filtering of its own on search results (autocomplete.js renders data.results directly), so this predicate is the product's search semantics.
assets/js/autocomplete.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
Changing substring to prefix matching, or to whole-word matching, alters what every user's search box finds — and autocomplete.js's debounced dropdown will look "broken" with no error anywhere. Matching against the un-lower-cased name would make searches case-sensitive on Linux but not Windows (their filesystems' toLowerCase behaviour differs), creating a platform-dependent bug that is brutal to reproduce.
💻 Live Source Code:
functionnameMatches(name,query){ if(!query)returntrue; returnString(name).toLowerCase().includes(query); }
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

sect2.title: 🧩 Function: searchEntries(projectRoot, query, options)
🧩 Function: listLatestReleases(projectRoot, limit)
🧩 Function: peekRootSync(projectRoot)
🧩 Block: module.exports
sect2.para:
🎯 Purpose
The module's public surface: the seven functions server.js is allowed to know about — the complete, frozen boundary between transport and domain layers.
🧒 ELI5
The basement door's service window. Exactly seven hatches are open; the librarian can shout through these and nothing else. Everything else in the room — helpers, constants, private tools — stays behind the wall.
⚙️ How It Works (Step-by-Step)
Export list: listCategories (→ /api/categories), listPath (→ /api/files), getDownloadTarget (→ /api/download), searchEntries (→ /api/search), listLatestReleases (→ /api/releases), peekRootSync (→ /api/health + banner), getRoot (exported for completeness/testing; no route uses it).
Deliberately not exported: isHidden, serviceError, resolveConfiguredRoot, splitRel, resolveInsideRoot, toPosixRel, readVisibleEntries, assertCategoryStructure, summarizeTree, nameMatches — all internal. This privacy is what makes the path-safety wall auditable: no caller can bypass resolveInsideRoot because no caller can reach anything that skips it.
server.js consumes this via const filesService = require("./lib/files-service") immediately after loadEnv(PROJECT_ROOT) — ordering that guarantees process.env.FILES_ROOT exists before the first call.
📥 Inputs
None.
📤 Outputs
The module's exports object, consumed by server.js.
🔗 Project Dependencies
Depends on: every function above.
Consumed by: server.js exclusively (verified: no other file in the repository requires this module).
server.js
⚠️ Breaking Change Warning
This object is the API between layers. Removing or renaming a key is a crash-at-boot (filesService.listCategories is not a function on the first matching request). Adding exports is safe but widens the trust boundary — anything exported must uphold the same validation guarantees. Note getRoot is exported though no route calls it: useful for tooling/tests, but any new route consuming it directly must remember it validates the root but not the category structure.
